title: AI assistance is leading to lower code quality, claim researchers
summary: Reports GitClear's analysis of rising code churn and copy-paste alongside AI adoption, set against GitHub's productivity claims.

assertions.quote: They also see an increase in churn, now at 7.1 percent compared to just 3.3 percent in 2020.
no greater scourge to long-term code maintainability.
suggestions for added code, but never suggestions for updating, moving, or deleting code.

verdicts.note: True of completion-style assistants and consistent with GitClear's falling moved-code share, but agentic tools now routinely refactor and delete code.

RefactoringMiner found AI-assisted developers did as many or more refactorings (mean 18.3 vs 15.4) but mostly simple ones such as Inline or Rename Variable. Non-AI developers did more structural moves (Move Method 1.89 vs 0.21). Refactoring was not discouraged overall, but the deeper kinds were rarer.

Across 302k real AI-authored commits, AI fixed slightly more static-analysis code smells than it introduced (439,817 vs 432,748), which suggests it does perform local cleanup. Smell removal is only a loose proxy for refactoring.
